evidence.note: Eight TaskCreate calls decompose the build into ordered subsystems: storage/SQLite-WAL/skeleton first, SigV4 second (hardest unknown front-loaded), then data plane, multipart/versioning, policy/cors/lifecycle, admin, console, and integration testing last — dependency-aware sequencing with foundations before dependents.
Repeated TaskUpdate in_progress/completed transitions show the milestone plan used as a living progress tracker spanning the full horizon, not a one-shot list.
A per-subsystem verification suite (t1 basic … t10 auth, plus concurrency/console-UI) provides concrete acceptance checks aligned to each milestone, effectively giving each subsystem a done-check.
Environment reconnaissance precedes decomposition, feeding the foundation-first ordering of the task plan.

reasoning: The agent created an explicit, dependency-aware milestone hierarchy that front-loads the highest-risk foundations (concurrency-safe WAL storage, byte-exact SigV4) before dependents like multipart and versioning, and tracked each milestone to completion — matching the level-8 anchor. Per-subsystem test files supply concrete acceptance checks. It falls short of 10 because acceptance criteria were not encoded per-milestone upfront and the plan was largely static rather than re-sized/re-sequenced as scope reality emerged.
